Sometimes they may be in concordance, but sometimes they are in deep collision. Sometimes you face a dilemma. You are either going to choose justice or peace. This Tribunal always avoided initiating a discussion on its legality. When this discussion started in the first proceedings here, that is to say, the trial of Dusan Tadic, as an interesting irony of history, the legality of this Tribunal was challenged by the current Judge, Alphons Orie, together with Attorney Wladimiroff. At that time, Orie was co-counsel in the Tadic case, and they, together, challenged the legality of the Tribunal. The Trial Chamber that decided on that inverted logic. They proved that the Tribunal was legal. They avoided a debate on illegality. An institutions whose legality is being challenged cannot decide itself on its own legality. It has to be someone else who is above that institution, and that could have been only the International Court of Justice, which is, regrettably, also here in The Hague. After this illegal Tribunal was established, and after its Statute was proclaimed in a resolution of the Security Council, the Judges of that Tribunal wrote the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence have to be fully in accordance with the Statute, and each and every one of its provisions has to be derived from the Statute. The Statute does not provide for a violation entitled "Contempt of Court." That was invented by the Judges, themselves, and it was incorporated in the Rules. It was first done on the 11th of February, 1994, and then it was changed/amended in 1995, and then 1997 twice, and in 2001. In the first version, it was possible to impose a maximum sentence of one year of imprisonment, then a year and a half, and ultimately it came up to seven years. So that was not done through the Statute. It was through the Rules that a new crime was brought in. In the contempt proceedings that were conducted, when that provision was challenged, the Trial Chambers of The Hague Tribunal concluded that that is the inherent power of the Tribunal. It is. In any court of law -- in any country in any court of law, it is the Court, itself, that decides whether there is contempt. It can be disciplinary measures. Sometimes, if there is witness intimidation, it can even be treated as a crime; a separate one, at that. Yes, authority is inherent, but the Court cannot, itself, prescribe the crime involved. The Court could have addressed the Security Council, asking to have the Statute amended. No one did that. It was the Judges, themselves, who willfully did that, because they thought that they were smart enough and capable enough to do that. That is how this new crime came into being, totally unknown in the Statute, at that. Of course, there is a justification for that. If certain sanctions can be imposed against a witness who refuses to testify, in modern legislation the law prescribes what kind of punishment can be meted out, and then the court of law, itself, says what the range is going to be in each and every particular case. Also, who refuses to appear before the Trial Chamber or who refuses to disclose certain documents can also be subjected to sanctions, but those prescribed by law, who intimidates witnesses, who tries to bribe a witness, or anyone else who has to do with the proceedings; trying to bribe a Judge, a Prosecutor, a lawyer, and so on. All of these crimes can be sanctioned exclusively by law. Now, what can the Court do? Just apply the law. Whereas here, it is the Court that creates the law and applies the law. There is no control over the judiciary here, even if it were a legal court, let alone the fact that it is not a legal court. As for the disclosure of information and the identity of protected witnesses, even common law and civil law know of the institute of witness protection. However, in your legal system, Mr. Morrison, or in your legal system, Mr. Hall - I did not study the South Korean legal system, so I don't know - there is no situation as follows: that the identity of witnesses is protected during testimony, or, rather, the public is never deprived of the right to know what the identity of a witness is. In civilised countries, the public may be kept out of a particular court case that have to do with marriage, rape, and other sexual crimes, and also in many cases of espionage. Quite a few countries in the world allow for that possibility, but the question remains whether that can be accepted as part of international customary law; that is to say, whether it has gone beyond that critical point of application in many countries so that it can be considered as part of international customary law. In civilised countries, it is the police that protects the sensitive witness, a witness who is in danger. It can be a witness who is a collaborator, who took part in the commission of a crime and then repented, or is part of a plea agreement in order to remain unpunished or with lesser punishment. However, the public does know who that witness is. The police protects that witness until the witness enters the courtroom. The witness testifies under his full name, in the presence of the public. Once that trial -- or, rather, once that testimony is over, if it is assessed that there is a danger involved, and nothing can be done without his consent, then his identity is changed, and his place of residence, and even the identity of his entire family, and then he is relocated so as to avoid the revenge of his former criminal friends or the mafia, who wishes to take its revenge against a witness who testified against them. It can also be a witness who was a victim, too, not necessarily one of their companions. In the civilised world, that is possible. However, The Hague Tribunal is not part of the civilised world. It is an institution that was established like the Inquisition in the Roman Catholic Church many years ago. It has a task before it, and then it is the duty of the Judges to discharge that task, and everything is subordinated to that, the Office of the Prosecutor and many Defence attorneys, almost all of those that are paid by the Tribunal, itself. This is what has been happening. In addition to resembling the Inquisition of the Roman Catholic Church, this Court resembles the Star Chambers Court of England which is several hundred years old. I think, Mr. Morrison, you know better than I do about this Court. This Court created rules as they went along ad hoc. So this is how the High Tribunal looks like. I was unfortunate enough to spend years here and to have an opportunity to study all of this, and I wrote a number of books. I'm not talking about the books where I ridiculed Judges and Prosecutors, et cetera. I'm talking about serious scientific books. And, that is, The Hague Prosecutors are not a match for me; neither are these witnesses brought here who just come here, and shine for a moment, and have no chance of out-shining me. What we have here is a proceedings for contempt of court, and there were several such proceedings. Some were tried for intimidating witnesses - I think his name was Beqaj, I think he was sentenced to five or six months in prison. He did not launch an appeal because he had already served that sentence. Some were tried for refusing to testify; for example, Ljubisa Petkovic in my case; Dragan Jokic, in the Popovic et al case. And also tried were people for unauthorised disclosure of confidential information. For example, some Croatian journalists published entire lists of witnesses from the Blaskic case and from other cases as well. The sentences pronounced were either up to four months in prison or token fines. I'm not telling you this because I am afraid of your sentence. You may easily sentence me to death. It is your right. You just get together and you do it quickly. To me, that would be an ideal end to my political and legal career. Therefore, I'm not interested whether you are going to sentence me to 15, 20, or I don't know how many years. My mission here is to disassemble The Hague Tribunal, and I have been doing that successfully for eight and a half years. I may continue to do so for another eight and a half years, until I have accomplished my mission, because that is my mission and that is my life, because I want to show to the world public that this is not the Court that operates according to the law, but under the dictate of major powers such as the US, the United Kingdom, the European Union and NATO. This is my objective, and I am going to achieve it. Now, in view of the proceedings conducted against me - actually, one of them has been finalised - I was sentenced to 15 months in prison. Why? Because in a book that contained 1200 pages, that had 2.400 journalistic pages, or columns, as journalists would call them, for having mentioned witnesses under code, and for having allusion to certain acts by certain people, so that someone who would read this book and scrutinize it in detail could arrive at a conclusion that, in fact, the man under a code-name is such-and-such person. In other words, I did not openly publish the names of protected witnesses. This huge book was perceived by the Trial Chamber as a puzzle that a smart and intelligent person can read and then reach conclusions as to the identity of the witnesses. Unlike those who were tried for divulging directly the lists of protected witnesses in the Blaskic case, or in other cases as well, and who received up to four months' sentences in prison or token fines, I was sentenced to 15 months, and I'm happy for that, because in front of the whole public -- world public, an unlawful act was committed, and a proceedings that is totally inappropriate was conducted especially for those who are jurists. In 2005, when I was first tried for contempt of court, proceedings were conducted simultaneously against Florence Hartmann. She had been the Prosecution spokesperson for several years. She published a book, and in that book she disclosed some strictly-confidential information that The Hague Tribunal had received under certain conditions from the pro-Western treacherous regime in Serbia, and that is to say, that this information can be used only in the trial against Slobodan Milosevic and that it should not be given to anyone else. Florence Hartmann published this in her book, and she was punished by a token fine imposed on her, even though her criminal offence is much more serious than anything that happened in The Hague Tribunal in the sphere of court contempt. She had abused her position that she held previously, because that was the only way she could have obtained those documents. Approximately at the same time, we both launched an appeal on sentence. My appeal was about 67 pages, because the Rules provide that appeals to first-instance judgement can contain up to 100 pages, whereas the appeal of Florence Hartmann was 92 pages' long, and I have it here. The Appeals Chamber accepted her appeal of 92 pages, whereas they returned my appeal with the instruction that I should reduce it to up to 30 pages because there was an internal enactment passed by the Tribunal President which provides that in case of court contempt, a number of pages of appeal must be reduced. You can see how strong this discrimination against me is. Now, about a month or two ago, The Hague Tribunal decided that all the documents that had been confidential and for which Florence Hartmann was sentenced, would now become public. They were first sent to the Muslim authorities in Sarajevo and then elsewhere. Florence Hartmann's appeal proceedings is still pending. Her appeal was launched on the 9th of October, 2009. After almost two years, the second-instance judgement was not passed yet, whereas in my case everything was done so expediently and expeditiously. Now, maybe, waiting to have all these documents in the public domain, she will receive even an even lesser punishment, which will amount, probably, instead of a couple of thousand Euros to a couple of hundred Euros. Now, this is what is undermining in this Tribunal in its very foundation, and I am delighted that this has occurred. Now, speaking about the subject of these proceedings: In 2009, proceedings were initiated by a Trial Chamber, in which Mr. Kwon sat as well, agreed to conduct these proceedings for this large book of 1200 pages, but they concluded that there were no sufficient conditions for proceedings to be conducted against the so-called books which I'm not going to mention by title in order to avoid the editing of the recording and the redaction of the transcript. The Trial Chamber has dismissed the application by the Prosecution for the lack of sufficient ground for instituting proceedings against Vojislav Seselj, because in the third book - and the third book is exactly this one, and Mr. Kwon knows that - divulged information by disclosing the names of witnesses and as the Prosecution requested. The Chamber had reason to believe that I knew that protected witnesses were in question. And now I'm citing paragraph 31: "Information from book number 3 indicate the identity of these persons only in terms of their being Defence witnesses. They are never mentioned as Prosecution witnesses, nor are their pseudonyms revealed ..." So this is the conclusion reached by the Trial Chamber, and I think that he was even the Presiding Judge. It seems that it is the destiny of Mr. Kwon to always sit on the Bench in my proceedings, so it seems that after all these proceedings, he is preparing to conduct the next one, until we reach number 10. I tried to apply for disqualification, I was not successful, and it seems that I cannot avoid looking at Mr. Kwon in at least eight new proceedings. I continue now with paragraph 31: "Therefore, the Chamber has no sufficient grounds to suspect that Seselj can be guilty of court contempt for having published, in his third book, such information on the basis of which it would be possible to identify these witnesses as protected witnesses for the Prosecution, contrary to the orders issued by the Trial Chamber in the Seselj case." Then the Prosecutor files an appeal with the Appeals Chamber. And I have been clashing with them for eight years already. I have mocked their names in public, through the titles of my books. So what was their ruling? They annul the decision of the Trial Chamber from 2009, and they order the initiation of contempt proceedings for this book. Mr. Morrison and Mr. Hall, I don't know what position you're going to take here. No matter how much the two of us hate each other, Mr. Kwon has to remain consistent with his decision from 2009. Nothing new appeared here that changes the factual situation that was well known in 2009, nothing new. The book was on an internet site then. Ten thousand copies of the book had already been sold then. The price was very low. I think it was 100 dinars per copy, because we didn't really want to make any money at all. We wanted it to reach the masses of people as soon as possible so that they would see what kind of proceedings are underway here against me and that compromise -- that actually give a bad name to the Tribunal and to the Trial Chambers who are trying me. We have a few other things involved here. In the main trial against me, more than half of the witnesses enjoyed protective measures. Some of them testified in completely closed session. I proved, very effectively, that they were false witnesses. Then, several months ago, I filed criminal complaints against 44 false witnesses from my case, 44 witnesses who appeared in court, testified, almost all of them under protective measures, some of them in closed session, and 4 persons that the OTP gave up on. The President of the Tribunal, Patrick Robinson, rejected my motion. He said that he was not the organ in charge. When I filed a criminal complaint against the former warden of the prison, Timothy McFadden, because he disclosed confidential information that had to do with the private life of Slobodan Milosevic, then Patrick Robinson was in charge, and he established a Trial Chamber that would look into the matter. That Trial Chamber was headed by Alphons Orie. I think that Moloto was one of the members, and I can't remember the third one. They haven't looked into the matter yet, but this is what was done. If, indeed, in this major case, involving 44 witnesses, it is only the Trial Chamber that is trying me that is in charge, then, Judges, what you are trying me for over these few days would also fall under that Trial Chamber. And why not? They didn't want to try me. They said to the President of the Tribunal that they would not be involved, so then the President appointed the initial Trial Chamber from 2009, and now they have appointed you. Sometimes it's like this, and sometimes it's like that. If what Patrick Robinson says in his response is true, then it wouldn't be Alphons Orie who would be in charge of McFadden, it would be the Judges who tried Slobodan Milosevic, because in that trial there was a breach of privacy. All the press wrote about that, and Wikileaks carried this information. Timothy McFadden informed the American ambassador in The Hague in writing about the private life and private situation of Slobodan Milosevic, which is absolutely forbidden, and that is much worse than all the things you refer to in Rule 77. Now let us see how these proceedings will end. Let's see what Alphons Orie is going to write in his report. I know in advance, but I don't want to say it. Maybe it wouldn't be fair. Some day, he will have to file that report. What is the main problem that appears in The Hague Tribunal? It is false witnesses. Proceedings take place here very easily because of the disclosure of confidential information, but no one has been tried because of false testimony. Mr. Kwon was a member of the Trial Chamber of Slobodan Milosevic, and he knows full well that it was established there that more than 50 witnesses, in their viva voce statements, completely denied the preliminary statements that were written up for them by the Prosecution after they were interviewed, over 50 of them. We had an example here as well. That is why I had to be a bit more flexible with regard to my basic principle not to question any witnesses who are testifying under protective measures. The witness I did examine here confirmed to you that he gave false testimony in the Milosevic case, and that he was forced to do so by the Prosecution. I expected you, Mr. Kwon, to react. I expected you to initiate proceedings because of that. Do you not agree that false testimony is a far more serious crime than disclosing protected information? There is no comparison between the two, in terms of the danger that threatens society. Draconic punishment is handed out by The Hague Tribunal primarily because of these false witnesses and false testimony; Milan Martic, Stanislav Galic, Dragomir Milosevic, Stakic, Brdjanin, and many others, Momcilo Krajisnik, and so on. I cannot even enumerate all of them, although I am familiar with all the cases. I have studied them all very thoroughly. They were sentenced to very high sentences because of false testimony, and no one was ever held responsible, none of these false witnesses. You know what the usual wording is when that happens? In the judgements, the Judges write and say, Well, yes, he did provide false testimony, he provided some unreliable information, but the rest is true. You have that particular wording in many, many judgements. Why? Because everyone here is aware of the fact that this is a mass occurrence, this false testimony, and nobody reacts to it. On the basis of my criminal complaint, a friend of the Court was established for the very first time. The 7th of October is the dead-line for him to look into the complaints that I filed against the Prosecution; that is to say, making people provide false testimony. Look at another thing that's very important here. The Trial Chamber in the main trial, the Trial Chamber that is presided over by Judge Antonetti and whose members are Flavia Lattanzi and Frederik Harhoff, they, themselves, provide this wording: "Every witness can ultimately decide whether he is going to testify before the Chamber without protective measures." That is their own principle of the 3rd of March, 2008. And then already in 2009 or 2010, they, themselves, violate that principle, and this very same witness, the first one that you sent back from here because he did not want to testify under protective measures, that's exactly how he fared during the main trial. What do these principles mean, then? What happened was that Zoran Drazilovic did not find this order sufficient, so with the assistance of his lawyer, he sent a request to the Trial Chamber that he be provided additional guarantees that once he came to The Hague, no one would impose protective measures on him. So on the 14th of March, an additional order was issued, stating guarantees to Zoran Drazilovic that no protective measures would be imposed upon him and that only the Chamber and the Registry and VWS would be the only ones to contact him while he is in The Hague. I assume that "VWS" stands for Victim and Witness Protection. Once I received this decision, there was no doubt in my mind to the effect that each and every one of these witnesses could decide to do away with his own protective measures. That is how I published the book. That does not mean that I would not have had the book published otherwise. I would have published that book one way or the other. However, I was relaxed because of this position taken by the Trial Chamber. That I was quite right was confirmed by the first Trial Chamber that made a decision on this, and Mr. Kwon was in that Trial Chamber too. Why did the Appeals Chamber do this? You see, in 2009, the Trial Chamber accepted the motion regarding three books, so the third one is the one that you are trying me for right now. Actually, had they agreed to that, then the proceedings would have been simultaneous with those for the book of 1200 pages. It would have to be the same. It's the same three books, plus one. However, first this draconic judgement is passed with regard to one book, and then two years later then proceedings are instituted with regard to another book. That can only happen in The Hague Tribunal. In the civilised world, that could not happen anywhere. Since no one wants to try false witnesses here, then I have to deal with them in public. The public is my only weapon. You see that no one who testified in proceedings against accused Serbs - it's not only me, all the Serbs here - no matter how much false testimony they provided, they had no problems whatsoever. People close to them could have despised them for it, could have stopped communicating with them, but their life was not at risk in any way. They were not facing any security risks, so there is no such danger involved. There is another danger, though, and in my case it is the danger of the Trial Chamber strangling me in the dark. Well, I'm not going to let them strangle me in the dark. My only protection before the Judges of The Hague Tribunal is the public, because I'm being tried by these Judges. It became obvious that they very rarely adjudicate on the basis of the law. It has been proven that this is a markedly anti-Serb tribunal. Look at the indictments here. Over 80 per cent of them were issued against Serbs. Less than 20 per cent are against Croats, Muslims, Albanians and Macedonians. It's an anti-Serb tribunal. They are trying to break the backbone of the Serb people. I'm not being tried here on account of any war crimes. I'm being tried here for ideology. Pursuant to Rule 98, although there was a very significant disagreement among members of the Trial Chamber and Judge Antonetti dissented, everything boils down to hate speech as a form of persecution. You know that incitement must be direct and must lead directly to the commission of a crime. Otherwise, if you do that in the media, it doesn't count. And, anyway, a hate speech does not figure as a crime in international law. You know that in Rwanda, there was incitement to genocide, which was depicted as hate speech. And on the basis of that, it was included in the Statute, only on the basis of public incitement to genocide. It is obvious that in the main trial, they have no grounds to convict me. Now, there is a whole series of proceedings for court contempt, in which I intend to participate very actively, and I will do that in a very patient way. I might seem to you as a nervous person, but I can tell you that I am very thorough and very patient. Once one proceedings is completed, I'm going to create conditions for the next one. As soon as we finish the next one, I'm going to prepare myself for the next one and the next one, up to 10. That's what I decided. And it's not my problem; it is your problem, how you're going to get away from that. What are you going to do if all the aggregate sentences for contempt of court in my case reach 10 years? I am a defiant person, and Mr. MacFarlane concluded that correctly, and I am proud of that characteristic of mine. As the great leader of the whole Korean people, Kim Jong-Il, said, Who fights for the truth, freedom and justice sincerely must be ready to sacrifice themselves. Now, as a follower of this thought of Kim Jong-Il, I am prepared to sacrifice myself. I am going to win. Even if I die, I will be the winner. Here, Mr. MacFarlane enumerated some six or eight submissions or theses, and I'm going to tackle a number of them. He mentioned aggravating circumstances, and he said that I did it on purpose. Of course I did. He said that that was a spiteful act. Of course it was, because I knew it was going to deliver a heavy blow on The Hague Tribunal, because this book is a testimony to what kind of court proceedings are being conducted in this Tribunal. Then he said that I was pretending the whole time. I never pretended. I always speak openly, and I speak my mind, and I am playing with my cards on the table. Why? Because I feel superior. I feel superior to all of you. You cannot suppress my feeling of superiority. No one can do that. You will have to find someone more intelligent than me, someone more educated than me, a better lawyer, and I never met such a person in my life. Okay, let's move on. Mr. MacFarlane also said, and that hurt a bit, that I engaged at least one of my relatives to run my internet site. That is not true. The chief editor of my internet site is my oldest son, Nikola Seselj, and I am proud of that. I am proud of his name and his participation in that, and that is the guarantee that no one will do anything there against my will. All the Tribunal orders would be in vain, and it cannot be shut down. First, they have tracked the provider in Sweden, and there was an order issued for the web site to be closed. I managed to find a provider in Germany. Then I found another one in Serbia. So my site was never shut down for more than 24 hours. Now I have a provider in California that ignores all kinds of orders. It seems that the State of California has a modern democratic order, and no courts in California will abide by any orders issued to them. And, therefore, my internet site is safe. The Tribunal cannot do anything against the State of California. They cannot even declare war on them. Therefore, my internet site will survive me, and everything posted there would never be removed. Mr. MacFarlane is talking some rubbish. He said that I was disingenuous. I don't know where he got this from. I have always been completely candid, even if that was to my disadvantage. He also said that I was arrogant and defiant. Yes, I am defiant, and I'm also arrogant. Why not? Anyone who is superior has the right to be arrogant. Only stupid people, it doesn't suit them to act arrogantly. As for those who are superior are fully entitled to act arrogantly. That is what is expected of them until someone more superior emerges. Try to find someone more superior to me. I think that you, yourselves, are disappointed in the capabilities of Mr. MacFarlane, and I hope that for the future proceedings, you're going to find a different friend of the Court, because I don't think it is appropriate, and it is very awkward to keep looking at Mr. MacFarlane getting entangled in his own words. And I hope you will find someone who would be a match for me as an adversary in this courtroom. Ms. Wanlin spoke about my web site. I am, as I said, proud of my son, Nikola Seselj, and his collaborators. He's not doing this himself, but he's my editor-in-chief. We have a developed network of links with other sites. Everything is delivered and distributed at lightning speed, and no one can shut us down. He also said that I pre-empted any bans that the Registry wanted to impose. That is true. Whatever the Registry tried to do, I already had a ready-made response, thanks to my son, Nikola, and his collaborator; immediately, automatically. And, of course, everything can be downloaded free of charge. I do not want to charge anyone for my struggle against The Hague Tribunal. I am fighting against this Tribunal to destroy it and raze it to the ground so that no one would ever decide again to establish such ad-hoc tribunals. I'm not concerned about my survival, but I do have ideals, I have my objectives. One of my political objectives is to destroy The Hague Tribunal with strong arguments. If you see the Tribunal as a tank, I'm going to jump in front of the caterpillar of that tank with an explosive, and that is my intention. I managed to do that to a great extent already, because nobody in the world believes that the proceedings, the main proceedings conducted against me are based on the law and the legal principles. All jurists worldwide realise my basic human rights have been violated. Nobody in the world can justify these court contempt proceedings. Nobody can justify the secrecy of proceedings. Various methods of manipulation have been developed in this Tribunal. These proceedings are very expensive, and none of the Serbs have so far been able to afford their own defence. And they say, Well, the Tribunal will cover the expenses. Yes, they will do so, but provided you choose a counsel from their own list, in which case the counsel works for the Tribunal, not for the defendant. We have the example of the first appearance -- initial appearance of the famous Serbian general, Ratko Mladic. Ratko Mladic stated that he hadn't seen the indictment, and then Judge Alphons Orie asked the standby counsel, appointed without the consent of Ratko Mladic, whether he read the indictment, and the counsel stood up and said, yes, he did. They're still keeping General Ratko Mladic in isolation in a darkened room, and I don't know who is going there to interview him, whether it's people from the Registry or from the Prosecution, but we see that something is going on. They are trying to achieve something while he is in isolation. But you will see how long it will take for him to create his Defence team. That is what they tried to do with me. As soon as I came here, Judge Schomburg imposed on me a standby Defence counsel. It took me four years to get rid of that standby counsel. First it was a Serb, then a Dutchman, and then immediately prior to the beginning of the trial, an Englishman was appointed as my Defence counsel, against my will. And I made so much effort to challenge and to reject that, so eventually they accepted all my requests. They changed the Trial Chamber, they dismissed all the standby counsel, that they allowed the visit of my spouse, Jadranka, and that I received all the papers and documents exclusively in the Serbian language. So all my requests have been granted. Once that was accomplished, I could hardly wait for the trial to begin. The trial is still in progress, because they're really finding it difficult to find what to charge me with. You will see for yourselves that you have nothing to find me guilty of. Now, this is a test of your conscience, whether you're going to pass a conviction and, in this way, deserve to take part in some other proceedings in the future, or whether you're going to acquit me and, in this way, have the Americans, NATO, the European Union, and many others put you in their bad books. So it's for you to decide. Mr. Kwon already gave himself a bad name in the previous proceedings. Mr. Morrison, Mr. Hall, are you going to do that? It is up to you. Now, what is it that matters to me? What I find important in these proceedings as well is to say whatever I had to say before the public. I'm pleased because of that. I just abhor the secrecy of any proceedings. As soon as I can say things in public, everything in public, I am quite satisfied, and I'm not interested in your judgement at all. Don't listen to Mr. MacFarlane. You don't want that kind of a pittance of a judgement. Give me a 30-year imprisonment or something like that. There were some judgements where the laws of Spain from the days of Franco, and the laws of South Africa in the days of apartheid, were referred to. You can find support for whatever you want to do anywhere, with Idi Amin, or Jean Bedel Bokassa I, or the Communist dictator, Tito, or Hitler, or Stalin. You know, Hitler may be the greatest criminal in the history of mankind; not maybe, but that is for sure. But Georgi Dimitrov was acquitted, even under Hitler, because he was found not guilty. That is not possible here. Only two Serbs were acquitted here just so that people could see that the Tribunal is capable of acquitting some Serb. That was the case of Major Radic, because they didn't manage to prove anything. They didn't manage to prove anything in the case of some others, but they were found guilty, nevertheless. Also, they acquitted Milan Milutinovic because, poor him, he was proving throughout the proceedings that he was clashing with Slobodan Milosevic at the relevant time, and the Trial Chamber accepted that. I read that in the judgement against the Serbian political and military leaders who were charged with alleged crimes in Kosovo and Metohija. That's it, that's the kind of tribunal this is. Is my hour about to expire now? Can somebody help me with this? Do I have any more time left? Do I have a little bit of time left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, please carry on. You passed -- or it's almost an hour, but it's up to you. I'm not limiting your time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. This is the first time that I have had a favourable surprise coming from your side, Mr. Kwon. However, I'm not going to abuse that. I am going to finish within three or four minutes. So these proceedings are being brought to an end, and these proceedings remain in history. One day, when someone impartial assesses all of these proceedings, then these people will be judging both you and me. That is the judgement of history or of science. That's what it's called. I am pleased by the fact that in the future, there will not be a single serious textbook in the field of law that will be written without referring to the proceedings against me here, and part of these criminal proceedings are these many contempt proceedings, some of which have already taken place, and others are yet to take place. In this case, the procedure is quite simple. Once a decision was made, and then it was sent back for a review - nothing happened in the meantime - all the witnesses explicitly said that they had revealed their own identity, there is no proof of me revealing the identity of protected witnesses, and so on and so forth. Now, what will the judgement of the public be? There are people who don't care about what the judgement of the public is. These are people who are usually considered to be anti-social, dishonourable, dishonest, et cetera. All honourable people set great store by their reputation, the judgement of the public, their morality. All honourable people set great store by their own dignity. My very personal feeling of dignity makes it incumbent on me to fight the new international order by all means; the American domination, NATO, the European Union, and The Hague Tribunal that is one of their criminal instruments. I'm going to do that at any cost, even my life, and you do whatever you please. To be quite frank, I'm not even interested in your judgement. The judgement that you are going to pass will some day be a judgement for you. Bear that in mind. That is what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. Do you have anything in rebuttal, Mr. MacFarlane?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: No, I don't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Just one short question, to which I hope there can be a short answer, Mr. Seselj. It's an entirely academic proposition, really. If the Tribunal, itself, can't create its jurisprudence, would you be suggesting that that was a function of the Security Council? And if so, would you be suggesting that the Security Council had a parliamentary function?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It pretended and acted as if it had a legislative role. But according to the Charter, it cannot have that kind of role, in terms of establishing institutions. It does have a certain legislative role, but that is strictly defined in the Charter. This legislative role of the Security Chamber is based on binding resolutions in order to establish peace, preserve peace, et cetera. However, there is no legislative role in the establishment of international courts, ad-hoc ones or permanent ones. The establishment of a real international criminal court, and the Rome Statutes, and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, demonstrated how this Court was supposed to be established, had it been done properly. The greatest negation of The Hague Tribunal is the permanent International Criminal Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise, and we'll set the date for the delivery of the judgement in due course. The hearing is now adjourned.
